questions.q: Why does the EDA chart label each bar with its group size and add an error bar?
options: To make the chart look more colorful
Because matplotlib requires it
A rate without its sample size and uncertainty can make a noisy difference look like a finding
To convert rates into counts
questions.explain: With groups of a few hundred customers and 15.4% churn, small gaps are often sampling noise. Group sizes and error bars show how much to trust each difference.

questions.q: The Premium plan churns at 21.4% and Family at 11.5%, with non-overlapping 95% error bars. What is the appropriate conclusion?
options: Premium and Family differ by more than sampling noise, so plan is a useful signal
The plan column is irrelevant
Premium causes customers to leave
The difference must be a data error
questions.explain: Non-overlapping intervals suggest a real difference in churn rates. It shows association, not that the plan itself causes cancellation.

questions.q: Region churn rates range from 14.2% to 16.0%, and every bar overlaps the 15.4% average. How should region be treated?
options: As the strongest feature
As a column carrying little or no signal, despite looking like a natural feature
As proof the data is clean
As a target variable
questions.explain: The differences are within noise. Not every plausible-looking column is predictive, and exploration is how you find that out before modeling.

questions.q: Customers with 18 or more months of tenure churn at 24.9%, versus 9.7% for those under 6 months. What does this tell you?
options: Long-tenured customers are always loyal
Tenure has no relationship to churn
Tenure was measured incorrectly
Long tenure does not protect against churn here, and a candidate explanation, such as more chances for bad deliveries, should be tested rather than assumed
questions.explain: The pattern is opposite to a common assumption. Exploration surfaces it and suggests hypotheses, such as the overlap with late-or-refunded share, that modeling and further analysis can examine.

questions.q: Newer customers with few late orders churn at 8.8%, and longer-tenured customers with more late orders churn at 27.3%. What does this show?
options: Tenure and late share are the same variable
The two signals each add risk and stack, so a model using both can outperform one using either
Late orders cause tenure
Churn is random
questions.explain: Crossing two factors reveals that risk rises with each, and roughly triples when both are present. That combined structure is what a machine-learning model can exploit.
